主要内容: The S&P/Case-Shiller Home Price Index is a widely used measure of the health of the U.S. housing market. It tracks changes in residential real estate values both nationally and in 20 metropolitan regions. The index is composed of several components, including the national home price index, the 10-city composite index, the 20-city composite index, and 20 individual metro area indexes. The 10-city composite index includes cities such as Boston, Chicago, Denver, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, South Florida, New York, San Diego, San Francisco, and Washington. The 20-city composite index includes these cities plus additional locations such as Phoenix, Tampa, Atlanta, Detroit, Minneapolis-St. Paul, Charlotte, Cleveland, Portland, Dallas/Fort Worth, and Seattle. The index was developed in the 1980s by Karl E. Case, an emeritus economics professor at Wellesley College, and Robert J. Shiller, an economics professor at Yale University. They created the repeat-sales method to analyze home price trends by comparing repeat sales of the same properties. The index is published on the last Tuesday of each month with a two-month lag. It is managed by Standard & Poor's and is available on their website. Options and futures based on the Case-Shiller Index are traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
